name: Club Shelf
idea: A book-club hub that works for the whole club even when members use different reading trackers: ranked polls, club TBR with votes, RSVPs and a club-wide ratings leaderboard.
description: Book-club organisers on StoryGraph keep asking for ranked or multi-pick polls, a shared club TBR members can upvote, several admins, club stats and a leaderboard that includes members who are not on the platform. Club Shelf is a standalone web app where the organiser creates a club, members join by link with no account, and each member can optionally upload their StoryGraph or Goodreads CSV export to prefill ratings and 'who has this on their TBR'. Voting maths (ranked choice, approval) and CSV-export parsing are the technical core.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, Supabase free for clubs/polls/RSVPs (row-level security per club), Open Library API for book covers, CSV parsing client-side; installable PWA.
why_hard_to_copy: Moderate at best: ranked-choice/approval voting correctness, tolerant parsing of StoryGraph and Goodreads CSV exports (edition-agnostic matching of books) and club-level stats are real work, but a basic polls-and-RSVP club app is weekend-copyable (Bookclubs already exists).

signals.summary: Official 'Book Clubs V2' request thread opened by the vendor; the board listing shows it as an Ideas-status item with 96 and 43 as its two counters (votes and comments, unlabeled) and the thread has 60+ replies of feature asks.
A club member asks for polls with more than 4 books, pick-3-of-8 voting, ranked-preference voting, and separate roles for members, mods and organiser, plus streaks for regular attendance.
Organiser wants several administrators and the ability to transfer ownership so a club keeps its history when a member steps back; a reply says co-admin help is what stops her starting a club.
signals.engagement: 7 likes on the post, 2 on the reply

signals.summary: Member asks for club book suggestions that use the members' past reviews, like the buddy-read recommender, to feed the next poll.

A large club migrated from Goodreads lists the gaps they hit: 5-book polls, notifications for all readalong posts, readalong dates vs single meeting date, club stats, club-run challenges and a ratings leaderboard that counts everyone regardless of when they read.

name: Pitch Plan
idea: Tournament-day and mini-league planner for youth clubs: fixtures across pitches and time slots, live standings with sport-specific tiebreakers, and a printable end-of-season report.
description: Parents and volunteer coaches running youth tournaments and small leagues ask their team-manager app for tournament mode, league tables, league-calendar import and a printable season report, and the vendor has kept those on 'planned' for a year or more. Pitch Plan generates round-robin and pool-plus-knockout schedules for several divisions sharing limited pitches, with rest-time and duplicate-opponent constraints, then publishes a public standings page and a one-page PDF season report. All solver and tiebreaker logic runs in the browser so it fits the free tiers.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel Hobby; scheduling solver in a Web Worker client-side; Supabase free stores tournaments and results; public read-only standings URL; print CSS for PDF report.
why_hard_to_copy: Constraint-based fixture scheduling (shared pitches, rest gaps, balanced home/away, multi-division) and per-sport tiebreaker rules are correctness-critical and fiddly; plain bracket makers are easy, a trustworthy multi-field scheduler is not.

signals.summary: Users want a Tournament activity with start/end time, meet-up time, description and a link to the tournament site (Tournify named); merged with an older duplicate in Jan 2026.
Coach asks for a fast way to enter other teams' matches so the team can see a league table; status Planned, and a second 'League table' request was merged into it on 2026-02-03.
Request to import the league's fixture list so all matches are added automatically; vendor moved it to In Progress on 2026-07-01 after two years.

Coach wants a customisable, printable A4 end-of-season report (form, home/away record, top scorers, awards, team colours); marked Planned on 2025-11-04 and the vendor said it would use the idea as input.

Mingle has no public API, so this is standalone, not an add-on.

name: Lesson Reflow
idea: A teacher pacing calendar where lessons flow forward day by day but chosen lessons stay locked to a date, with holidays, in-service days and A/B or weekend schedules handled.
description: Teachers and homeschoolers on Common Curriculum have asked for a decade to pin a test, assembly or live lesson to a date while the other lesson cards bump forward around it. Lesson Reflow is a drag-and-drop pacing calendar: the user defines the school calendar (breaks, in-service days, rotating day cycles, weekend classes), places unit and lesson cards, locks some to dates, and the rest reflow automatically when a day is lost. Copying a semester forward to next year re-snaps to the new calendar.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel Hobby; reflow engine runs client-side and works offline via service worker; Supabase free for accounts and plans; PDF/ICS export via browser APIs.
why_hard_to_copy: The reflow engine (locked items, skipped days, rotating day cycles, split periods, year-to-year re-snap) is correctness-critical calendar logic; plenty of planner CRUD apps exist but few handle locking plus bumping correctly.

signals.summary: Teacher again begs for a lock feature; a homeschooler (2025-11-19) wants live lessons locked to a day while other lessons are pushed forward, and another (2025-11-12) notes it has been asked for ten years.
Teachers with Saturday or Sunday classes cannot schedule them in the planner, which assumes Monday to Friday.
Teachers want to copy a week, month or semester of lessons into next year or the second semester and tweak it instead of retyping.
